description: Every Lua, JavaScript, Python, and visual case must resolve to exactly one realism class. Real-coverage validators use versioned named outcome contracts, never source substrings. Private paths, titles, covers, and book hashes remain in ignored build output.

real-epub-behavior.description: The companion opens or downloads the selected real EPUB and asserts document-derived behavior.

real-metadata-layout.description: The companion renders normalized embedded metadata or covers extracted from a real EPUB.

fixture-independent-control.description: The control is book-independent and an EPUB cannot affect the exercised path.

pure-logic-not-epub-dependent.description: The case deliberately isolates a pure algorithm, persistence rule, or boundary contract.

synthetic-pathology-with-real-companion.description: A minimal fixture pins a pathology while a real ReaderUI companion guards messy EPUB behavior.

real-server-contract.description: The contract is paired with the pinned real Grimmory compatibility lane.

non-epub-format-contract.description: The behavior is specific to PDF/CBX and cannot be validated by the eight EPUB assets.

externalRules.rationale: These fast Node tests isolate browser-oracle arithmetic, exact metadata/search projection, and checkpoint rejection; live Grimmory and real EPUB behavior remain in the full-server browser journeys.
These Python cases validate deterministic fixture, lifecycle, policy, report, and oracle tooling; live user outcomes remain owned by their versioned runtime contracts.

luaRules.rationale: These cases isolate strict DTO, displayed-description, result-set, card-association, live-DTO genre projection, and same-block inline-selection oracles; the full server and ReaderUI acceptance lanes consume the same exact contracts with real runtime books.
These cases isolate annotation field conversion and three-way planning behind an explicit CFI interface; ReaderUI annotation journeys are separate integration validators.
These cases pin URL normalization, HTTP framing, DTO parsing, error typing, and byte streaming; they do not claim that canned bytes form a readable EPUB.
The FIFO executor, cancellation, error delivery, and JSON sanitization paths do not inspect books or documents.
Minimal XML fixtures make individual CFI failures diagnosable; the real ReaderUI journey generates and consumes genuine CFIs across the private EPUB matrix.
This is a source-level gettext shadowing regression and no EPUB data enters the checked code path.
These cases pin destination sanitization and durable registry ownership; readable-byte download, hash, register, and open is a separate real-EPUB journey.
Account-scoped JSON persistence and legacy migration are independent of EPUB structure or reader behavior.
Authentication dispatch, token rotation, account storage, and async result application are independent of book contents.
Payload validation, duration thresholds, retry identity, and durable queue isolation are pure state rules; ReaderUI lifecycle capture is validated separately.
The safety algorithm intentionally injects ReadCollection and realpath so ownership, idempotence, and manual-item preservation can be proven without mutating a user's collections.

luaRules.rationale: The remaining cases isolate HTTP payload validation, account ownership, refresh behavior, durable queue races, and failure gates rather than document navigation.

luaRules.rationale: Fake ReaderUI cases make timing and gates deterministic; the companion opens real multi-document EPUBs and validates document-derived pull, jump, push, and clean repeat-sync behavior.
These parameterized cases cover PDF and CBX page positions; an EPUB companion cannot validate their page-based reader engines.
Badge geometry and aggregation of durable progress, annotation, and session state are presentation-model rules independent of document parsing.
Package extraction and daemon command orchestration are network-platform behavior and never inspect a book.
Archive validation, checksum enforcement, paired interruption recovery, rollback, and uninstall behavior are independent of EPUB assets.
Sort, filter, facet, bucket, and registry functions operate on normalized DTO values; real embedded metadata layout is covered by the private visual companion class.
